items.title: What Universities Say They Are For
items.researchQuestion: How has the public language universities use to describe their purpose changed over time?
items.firstRunnableBuild: Run current-page fetch, Wayback snapshot fetch, report build, audit packet, and readiness gate.
items.publicationAngle: A longitudinal essay about the movement from truth/civic language toward innovation, impact, global, and inclusion language, with careful source-layer caveats.
qualityRisks: Wayback coverage is sparse for exact current URLs
mission pages move or split across about/value/strategic-plan pages
short archived pages can produce false term drift

items.title: The Rise Of AI And The Humanities
items.researchQuestion: What are scholars publishing about AI, computation, archives, and quantitative methods in humanities-facing fields?
nextSources: JSTOR Data for Research where permitted
items.firstRunnableBuild: Run humanities literature radar pipeline with broad 2020-present source limits, normalize works, build report, and run readiness gate.
items.publicationAngle: A field-map essay showing where AI and quantitative methods are already entering humanities work, what corpora are being used, and which study directions look underexplored.
qualityRisks: metadata coverage underrepresents books and chapters
recent-year indexing lag can look like intellectual decline
keyword searches can overrepresent AI-explicit work and miss implicit computational methods

items.title: The Language Of Museums After Decolonization
items.researchQuestion: How have museums changed public language around civilization, world culture, provenance, restitution, repatriation, and decolonization?
items.unitOfAnalysis: museum page or annual-report section snapshot
nextSources: exhibition catalogs where metadata is public
items.firstRunnableBuild: Current-page source probe exists for 14 museums. Next build should add provenance, exhibition, collection, annual-report, and Wayback source layers.
items.publicationAngle: A longitudinal institutional-language essay about how museums publicly explain ownership, culture, world history, and repair.
qualityRisks: page redesigns can change text independently of institutional ideology
annual reports and exhibition pages represent different genres
some museums expose rich collection APIs while others expose only web copy

items.title: Canon Drift: A Feasibility Report
items.researchQuestion: Which sources can credibly measure changes in assigned, anthologized, cited, translated, or held authors over time?
items.unitOfAnalysis: author-work appearance in a syllabus, anthology, citation graph, translation record, or library-holdings record
items.firstRunnableBuild: Probe each source type for one author cohort and one institution cohort, then produce a matrix of measurable canon signals and coverage risks.
items.publicationAngle: A methods-forward public essay explaining what canon drift can and cannot be measured from public data before making large claims.
qualityRisks: syllabi are not a representative sample of teaching
library holdings measure acquisition and preservation, not readership
anthology editions require careful edition-level normalization

items.title: What Counts As A Humanities Dataset?
items.researchQuestion: What reusable corpora could support new quantitative humanities essays, and which are ready for immediate analysis?
items.firstRunnableBuild: Run a research scout over known corpus registries, audit the top 25 candidates, and rank them by access, coverage, licensing, and essay potential.
items.publicationAngle: A practical field guide to humanities datasets that can become public essays, not just academic infrastructure.
qualityRisks: licenses may allow inspection but not republication
corpora may require domain-specific normalization before they are analytically useful
